subject.title: feat: add tools.fs.roots — per-agent filesystem roots with access modes

question: Should OpenClaw accept `tools.fs.roots` and the new plugin SDK media helper as supported filesystem/media access policy surfaces after the explicit-root widening bug is fixed?
rationale: The PR creates a new operator-facing security boundary and plugin-facing API, so automation can repair the concrete bug but cannot choose the permanent product contract alone.

options.title: Accept after root-boundary repair
options.body: Fix the workspace-widening defect, keep the new config/API surface, and require focused tests plus refreshed merge proof before landing.

options.title: Keep core lean
options.body: Close or pause this PR and route the use case to an existing narrower media-root or plugin-owned capability instead of adding a broad core filesystem policy.

options.title: Narrow the API first
options.body: Remove or hide the plugin SDK export until maintainers explicitly approve the long-term plugin contract.

recommendation.title: Accept after root-boundary repair
recommendation.body: Fix the workspace-widening defect, keep the new config/API surface, and require focused tests plus refreshed merge proof before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-media and filesystem policy history points to this owner as the best available routing target for the root-boundary decision.
